Mutation-checked: disabling the class-rank rule fails 4 C11 tests, disabling concurrency-conflict detection fails 5 — the assertions discriminate.

Design points the lead should know:
1. Two delivery axes, not one. journal.state carries the admission ladder; outbox rows carry exported/transferred per transport with attempts + uncertainty windows. DELIVERY_TRANSITIONS has no local_persisted -> admitted edge, so a producer's own event cannot reach its own projection under the table as written.
2. Capability failure is terminal (rejected:unauthorized, per X-4) ONLY when a membership exists and denies. With no membership admitted yet it is retryable-quarantined, because "the policy has not arrived" and "the policy refuses" are different answers; conflating them makes admission depend on delivery order and breaks C16 plan B / C11 O2. This also means a fixture MUST make the membership a causal ancestor of anything it authorizes.
3. Admission order deviates from X-4 in one place: parents/relation-endpoints are checked BEFORE capability. Evaluating capability against a projection that is missing its policy manufactures a permanent refusal.
4. Delivery receipts live in an append-only store/receipts.jsonl that rebuild() replays, because C10 A18 / C09 A21 / C14 A-RCP3 / C16 A3.5 all require receipts to survive the loss of the derived index, and the index is where the ADR puts them.
5. archived is a FLAG beside an untouched status (archived_from recorded). C16 A2.1/A2.2 require exactly that, and it makes "restore never resurrects revoked authority" fall out of the representation instead of needing a guard.
6. reinstated refuses on a revoked/tombstoned/retracted record, recorded as a visible contested annotation. Without that guard C14 N2 (an immediate-rejection condition) fails.
